items.headline: NSW tribunal orders SIRA to reconsider releasing how icare's monopoly premiums are calculated, while shielding the insurer's internal numbers
items.summary: The NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal, ruling on 29 June on an access application by a law firm, found that information about how premiums are calculated in the SIRA-administered home building compensation scheme should be disclosed given long-running public concern about high premiums under a single-insurer monopoly, but that icare's internal profits, specific costs and business planning should stay confidential. Rather than order release, the tribunal sent the decision back to SIRA to reconsider in line with its reasons, with a directions hearing set for 7 July.
items.so_what: Although this concerns the home building compensation scheme rather than workers compensation, it is a transparency precedent on the same regulator: it narrows SIRA's ability to keep regulator-held insurer premium-methodology data confidential, and the tribunal's reasoning — that SIRA's compulsory information powers mean disclosure won't chill supply — could read across to future access requests over Nominal Insurer premium filings, especially with the icare premium target under a legislated freeze and public scrutiny of scheme pricing running high. Worth monitoring the 7 July directions hearing.

items.headline: EML white paper puts a 247% return-to-work figure on better claims handling as psychological-claim cost migrates across schemes
items.summary: A new EML white paper argues that three practical claims-handling steps — providing psychological and vocational support at first contact rather than after a liability investigation, warm handovers between workers-comp, income protection and social security with a single accountable case lead, and measuring success by recovery rather than by closing the file — rarely happen together across the system. It cites an independent Taylor Fry evaluation, published by Comcare, finding participants in one program were 247% more likely to return to work within six months, and models income-protection lodgements inside superannuation rising around 19% over a decade as Victoria and NSW tighten psychological-injury access.
items.so_what: This is the operational, provider-side complement to the cost-displacement thesis flagged earlier in the week: it reframes claims-handling quality and early intervention as direct levers on claim duration, premiums and cross-scheme cost migration, which matters for judging whether NSW's tightened psychological gateway and two-year premium freeze translate into genuine cost reduction or merely shift cost into super and TPD. A national read-across for NSW insurers and agents now operating under the new return-to-work-focused settings.
